headline: High risk: Langflow’s unsandboxed server-side execution and broad egress can turn Great Expectations outputs into unsafe actions, with shared-file and compliance leakage pathways.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Great Expectations can read and write validation files, while Langflow can ingest uploaded files and chain tools in flows. If Great Expectations output is copied into a Langflow flow or shared workspace, prompt-like content could be treated as instructions. No direct shared channel is documented, so this is inferred and uncertain.
conditions: IF Great Expectations outputs are manually pasted or uploaded into a Langflow flow
IF a shared filesystem or file-sync bridge is configured between the two agents
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Disable file upload ingestion in Langflow flows that consume GE outputs
Add a manual review step before any GE report is used as flow input
Use read-only exports for validation results
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between producer and consumer

B_data_leakage.rationale: Great Expectations touches validation results and documentation, and Langflow stores flow inputs/intermediate outputs while also handling per-flow credentials. If they share a workspace, Langflow’s broad egress can transmit copied data to external model providers or HTTP services. The pairwise leakage path is plausible but not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF both agents can read the same filesystem or uploaded artifacts
IF Langflow flows send those artifacts to external model providers or HTTP services
mitigations: Separate sensitive validation artifacts from Langflow workspaces
Restrict Langflow flows to local-only components
Rotate or remove credentials from flows that ingest GE outputs
Review outbound connectors before running shared-data flows
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention controls on flow inputs

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Great Expectations can install packages and write validation artifacts, while Langflow can execute shell commands, spawn subprocesses, write the filesystem, and run unsandboxed Python code server-side. On a shared directory, both can mutate files concurrently, and Langflow’s server-side execution makes the blast radius potentially irreversible. The interaction is dangerous by default if co-located.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same directory or repository
IF Langflow Python components are enabled in the flow
mitigations: Use separate directories for each agent
Disable Langflow Python code components for shared projects
Run one agent at a time when mutating shared files
Snapshot the workspace before executing flows
requires-engineering: add file locking or transactional writes

D_cascading_error.rationale: Great Expectations produces validation results that Langflow can chain into downstream agents or tools. Because Langflow supports graph-based flows and tool wiring, it may treat GE outputs as authoritative without a verification gate, causing bad validation conclusions to trigger downstream actions. The pairwise pathway is default-plausible and can propagate errors widely.
conditions: IF Langflow nodes consume Great Expectations validation output as a decision input
IF downstream flow steps act on that output without an explicit verification node
mitigations: Insert a human approval step before action nodes
Require schema checks on GE outputs before use
Log and diff validation results before downstream execution
Limit downstream nodes to read-only summarization
requires-engineering: add confidence thresholds and provenance checks

E_compliance.rationale: Great Expectations handles validation results and documentation, while Langflow stores flow inputs, intermediate outputs, and per-flow credentials. If regulated data is validated in GE and then moved into Langflow’s server-side flows with broad egress, retention and residency controls may diverge. The profiles do not show a specific jurisdiction mismatch, so this is a policy-gap risk rather than a confirmed breach.
conditions: IF regulated data or secrets are included in Great Expectations artifacts
IF Langflow retention or outbound connectors are not aligned with the source policy
mitigations: Classify which GE artifacts may enter Langflow
Set shorter retention on Langflow flow logs and stores
Exclude secrets from imported validation artifacts
Review residency and DPA requirements before deployment
requires-engineering: implement policy-based routing for regulated data
